issues: Travel occurrence, journey count/frequency, duration abroad, economic benefit, destination, transportation mode and life-hazard are different targets, not interchangeable successes.
Moon and Mercury receive priority in the source, but one early original aspect glyph between reception and first/ninth lord is still unclear.
Solar reception and conjunction branches, Moon/Mercury reciprocal domiciles and ninth/first lord placements are multiple alternative potential travel indicators.
Travel no/rare/many continuous and movable/fixed signs lack exact event count, calendar age, duration or economic profit thresholds.
Original compass planet mapping is Sun/Saturn East, Venus South, Jupiter North, Mars/Moon West; Mercury is conditional on aspects and may be neutral when conjunct luminaries without dignity.
Elemental signs represent Fire East, Air West, Earth South, Water North, which can contradict the planetary direction and other testimony.
Ptolemy-attributed source instead uses natal Sun/Moon Oriental/Occidental houses and permits East/Southeast versus West/North respectively; original Ptolemy text not yet independently collated.
Lilly then uses Mars/Moon celestial ecliptic latitude to propose North/South directions; opposite latitudes and contradictory compass indicators lack a prescribed solution.

The author's simple majority instruction does not specify eligible-indicator weights, ties, dominant region or no-prediction threshold. Retroactive choice among seven methods would make success claims meaningless.
Land versus water branches overlap with water-or-land permissive case and historical horse/coach/on-foot categories. These are not uniquely equivalent to modern multimodal transport or flight.
No complete astrological directional calculation, forecast window, country geometry, signifier-selection precedence or real travel itinerary data were used.
Dangerous travel, relocation wealth and religious beliefs are unsupported high-stakes or personal hypotheses, not actual individual forecasts.
Original printed CHAP CXL on causes of travel begins on PDF643 after CXXXIX mode subsection ends PDF642. This source must not absorb next chapter.
Historical source paragraph anchors are selective paraphrases not a complete diplomatic first-edition glyph-by-glyph transcription.
